title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Choppy Friday the 13th: Nvidia shake-up meets a 5% yield wall
conditions.summary: Futures are mixed and quiet ahead of October PPI, with the 10-year yield above 5% and December rate-hike bets running high. Nvidia's leadership change and a bitcoin slide set a cautious tone.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: S&P 500 futures are up about 0.1%, Dow futures up about 0.2%, Nasdaq-100 futures down about 0.1%; early quotes are thin and varied across sources.
Russell 2000 futures are up about 0.1% after small caps fell 1.7% on Thursday.
Thursday close: S&P 500 -0.35%, Dow -0.36%, Nasdaq -0.39%.
The 10-year Treasury yield is near 5.10%, its highest since October; the dollar index is near 103.1.
WTI crude is near $88 (-0.6%); gold is near $3,900 (+0.4%) but down over 4% on the week.
Bitcoin fell about 6.6% to near $68,700, below $70,000 for the first time since August; VIX is near 18.4.
Asia: Nikkei up under 1%, Hang Seng down about 1.5-2% on tech weakness, Kospi slightly lower.
Europe: Stoxx 600, DAX and FTSE 100 are modestly higher after the Stoxx 600 hit a record Thursday.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: 7:30 AM CT: October PPI, consensus +0.4% m/m (prior +1.3%), about 6.6% y/y; core consensus +0.3% m/m.
8:10 AM CT: Boston Fed's Susan Collins speaks; 9:50 AM CT: Fed Governor Michelle Bowman speaks.
Futures markets price high odds of a Fed rate hike at the Dec. 9 meeting, with some talk of a half-point move.
Main story: strong October payrolls and a hot CPI have flipped rate bets toward hikes and pushed the 10-year above 5%.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Cisco (CSCO): sales of about $18.1B beat estimates and full-year guidance was raised, but order growth slowed to 21%; shares are slipping in early trading (reports vary).
Applied Materials (AMAT): Q4 adjusted EPS of $4.16 beat; Q1 revenue guide of about $11.1B topped the $10.89B estimate; shares roughly flat.
Cerebras raised its 2026 revenue outlook; shares rose about 17% after hours.
After today's close: a light slate; next week brings Nvidia (Tuesday) and Walmart.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: NVDA (Nvidia): about +2.5% early — rebounding after Thursday's 4% drop on CEO Jensen Huang's resignation; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO.
MOD (Modine Manufacturing): about +27% after hours — report that Samsung is in talks to acquire it.
CBRS (Cerebras): about +17% after hours — raised 2026 revenue forecast.
CSCO (Cisco): about -2% — slower order growth despite a sales beat and raised guidance.
MSFT (Microsoft): about -2% — ongoing Outlook and Teams outage.
AMAT (Applied Materials): roughly flat — upbeat outlook largely priced in after a 41% year-to-date run.

sections.title: Business News
items: Nvidia is searching for a permanent CEO; a Senate committee chair has asked Huang and the Commerce Secretary to testify in December.
Microsoft's Outlook and Teams outage that began Thursday afternoon remains a focus for business users.
Oil stays supported as the US keeps its Iran blockade in place and Strait of Hormuz risks linger.
Crypto is under pressure, with bitcoin and ether each down more than 5% overnight.
Agile Robots raised $500M in a round led by SoftBank at an $8.5B valuation.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 7:30 AM CT: October PPI — a hot reading could add to December rate-hike bets.
The 10-year yield around 5.1% — whether it holds above 5% sets the tone for growth and tech stocks.
Nvidia's trading ahead of next Tuesday's earnings and its CEO search.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Friday, November thirteenth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. Friday the thirteenth, and my co-anchor isn't superstitious one bit. Gus the wonder dog, give the Dawn Patrol a lucky howdy! Let's check the swell. Futures are mixed and choppy early. S and P 500 futures are up about a tenth of a percent, Dow futures up about two tenths, and Nasdaq 100 futures are down about a tenth. Small caps are a touch higher. These early quotes are thin, so expect some shifting. The ten year Treasury yield is sitting around five point one percent, its highest since October. The dollar is firm, crude is near eighty eight dollars, and gold is up a bit near thirty nine hundred. Bitcoin had a gnarly wipeout, down more than six percent overnight to below seventy thousand dollars. Overseas, Tokyo's Nikkei gained, Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell more than one and a half percent on tech weakness, and Europe is slightly higher. Now the wind and weather. The October producer price index lands at seven thirty A M Central. Economists expect a rise of four tenths of a percent on the month, and three tenths on the core. Fed speakers follow, with Susan Collins at eight ten A M Central and Michelle Bowman at nine fifty. Hot jobs and inflation numbers have traders betting heavily on a Fed rate hike in December. On the tide chart, Cisco beat on sales and raised its full year outlook, but slower order growth has the stock slipping a couple of percent. Applied Materials gave a stronger than expected forecast, and shares are roughly flat. In the lineup, the big story is Nvidia. Jensen Huang has stepped down as chief executive, and finance chief Colette Kress is interim C E O. The stock fell about four percent Thursday and is bouncing a couple of percent early, with earnings due next Tuesday. Modine Manufacturing jumped about twenty seven percent after hours on a report that Samsung is in talks to buy it. Now that's how you hang ten! That earns a treat, Gus! Here you go, buddy! Chip maker Cerebras, still a grom on the market, rose about seventeen percent after raising its revenue forecast. Microsoft is lower as an Outlook and Teams outage drags on. On beach talk, oil stays in focus as the Iran blockade continues, and robotics firm Agile Robots raised five hundred million dollars in a round led by SoftBank. Sets to watch today: the producer price report at seven thirty, the Fed speakers, and whether the ten year yield holds above five percent. Soul surfers, stay patient out there; this market is all about rates right now. Got a stock, E T F or futures contract on your mind?
